summary: The Flutter workplace plus a display: everything from dev-flutter, the Linux desktop toolchain, and a virtual screen rendered in software, so a Flutter application can be run natively and operated through its VM service.

tools.name: flutter
tools.note: the SDK from dev-flutter, in /opt/flutter, with the Linux engine already fetched: `flutter build linux` and `flutter run -d linux` work without a download. `flutter --version` is the authority on the version.

tools.name: dart
tools.note: the SDK's own; `dart mcp-server` is the Dart MCP server

tools.name: Xvfb
tools.note: the virtual display. DISPLAY=:99 is already set; start the screen once per wake with dev start {"name":"display","cmd":"Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1280x800x24 -nolisten tcp"}

tools.name: xvfb-run
tools.note: for a one-off command that needs its own display, e.g. a test run

tools.name: xdpyinfo
tools.note: answers once the display is up — check it before you start the application

tools.name: clang, cmake, ninja, pkg-config
tools.note: the native toolchain a Linux desktop build needs, with GTK 3

tools.name: fvm
tools.note: only for a project that pins another version

tools.name: chromium
tools.note: headless, for the browser plugin and the web target

sdk_dirs.fvm: ~/fvm — only versions you asked for yourself
sdk_dirs.pub: ~/.pub-cache/bin is on the PATH, also for MCP servers the runtime starts: a tool activated with `dart pub global activate` is found there from your next run on

notes: Run the application natively to operate it: `flutter run -d linux` as a dev job, after the display is up. The VM service URI it prints is what marionette or the Dart MCP server connect to; with a recipe, covey/env_status reports it for a start entry whose control is `flutter`.
There is no GPU. Rendering is Mesa in software — correct, and slower than on a developer's machine. Judge animations by their end state, not by their frame rate.
No Android SDK and no emulator: a sandbox gets no /dev/kvm. A device test is a case for a human.
You are not root and apt is not available to you. If a tool is missing, say so instead of building a way around it — that is a request, not a defeat.
